default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-318.title: Record-pullback dip buy on a trend day
E-318.hypothesis: On a day already moved more than usual from the open, a pullback that first becomes deeper than every earlier pullback of the session triggers the trailing stops of the day's holders all at once; that forced selling is absorbed by the participant still driving the day, so buy the record pullback (mirror on a down day).

E-319.title: Dollar-at-extreme climax index break fade
E-319.hypothesis: A WIN break to a new short-term low while WDO sits at its own session high means both legs of the risk-off trade are stretched at once: the foreign desks' hedges are already in, the last sellers are the late locals, and macro dealers stop adding at the dollar extreme; fade the WIN break (mirror).

E-320.title: Yesterday's same-minute price poke fade
E-320.hypothesis: Day traders compare today's tape with where the market stood at the same time yesterday (overlay charts, intraday P&L versus a day ago); after price has stayed on one side of yesterday's same-minute price, a bar that pokes through it and closes back meets those anchored orders, so trade away from it.

E-321.title: Falling-participation micro-break fade
E-321.hypothesis: When the volume of the last window is clearly below the volume of the window before it today, the participants who were trading are leaving; a 15-minute break in that fading tape has no new size behind it and liquidity providers lean it back, so fade it (today's own volume decay, not the seasonal clock).

E-322.title: Widest-bar extreme poke fade
E-322.hypothesis: Today's widest bar is the session's biggest one-shot burst; its high and low are where that burst met the resting orders that stopped it. A later bar that pokes through that extreme and closes back meets the same untouched liquidity, so the poke buyers (sellers) are trapped; trade away from the level.

E-323.title: Yesterday's VWAP cross follow
E-323.hypothesis: Yesterday's full-session VWAP is the average cost of yesterday's inventory; after price has stayed on one side of it for a while, a close across puts that whole cohort from in-profit to under water (or the reverse), and their exits plus swing traders' entries push price on; follow the cross.

E-324.title: Volume-decoupled tape micro-break fade
E-324.hypothesis: Normally bigger price steps come with more volume (information moves price with size); when the recent correlation between absolute bar moves and bar volume is low, price steps are made by quote shifts, not by committed size, so a 10-minute break then is noise that liquidity providers fade.

E-325.title: Dollar session-average flip, index follows
E-325.hypothesis: When the dollar, after trading on one side of its own session average price for a while, crosses back through it, the day's FX flow has turned (foreign money now leaving or entering); equity desks act on the same flow a little later, so trade WIN against the dollar's flip.

E-326.title: Morning-range afternoon break fade
E-326.hypothesis: The 09:00-12:00 range is where the cash session's institutions did the day's main trade; an afternoon close beyond it is usually carried by the thinner afternoon crowd, while the morning participants hold their orders at their own range edges; fade the afternoon break back into the morning range.

E-327.title: Contained impulse bar fade
E-327.hypothesis: A bar much wider than usual for its minute and almost all body that still stays inside the last 30 minutes' range hit the book hard without reaching any level where stops or breakout orders rest; with nothing to cascade, the aggressor's push is the whole move and market makers re-centre; fade it.
